learning: Span, footprint, mass, body length and forward offset have all been tested at 12 mm in earlier races. Track width is now the untested single lever. Reading the next race: if line losses fall and steering_oscillation drops, turn rate was the limit. If line losses rise, the wider track is under-turning the sharpest bends.
notes: Iteration 9 package: the Builder's wheel_track test (0.12 to 0.14 m) on the iteration 6 best design (70.83). The controller is identical to iteration 6, so any score change is attributable to track width.
rationale: The Builder's iteration 9 proposal is the iteration 6 design (score 70.83) with one change: wheel_track 0.12 m to 0.14 m. Evidence: iteration 6 left one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error 0.0641 and 0.0669 m and low steering_oscillation (0.133 and 0.148). Iterations 7 and 8 closed the footprint and span levers at 12 mm: the 8 mm footprint scored 67.75 and the ±0.04 m span scored 36.6. Iteration 5 showed that a shorter body hurts, and iteration 3 showed that a forward offset does not remove the loss. Yaw inertia is already at the 0.4 kg floor, so turn rate is the remaining untested lever. Turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a 0.14 m track gives about 14 percent less turn per unit of PWM differential. The effective steering gain therefore falls with the track change. I keep the iteration 6 controller exactly (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights +1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1) so that the race isolates the track change. Raising kp to offset the lower turn rate would confound the test. Geometry is passed through as the Builder specified: 0.4 kg, body 0.16 m by 0.12 m, five sensors at x = +0.03 to -0.03 with y = 0.05 m, 12 mm footprints, wheel_radius 0.03 m. Expected result, as a prediction only: steering_oscillation at or below about 0.15, and line losses at or below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom. The main risk is that slower turning causes an earlier line loss on the sharpest bends, which would show up as a lower score.
